source_text: Regnavit - inquit - mors etiam in eos, qui non peccaverunt in similitudine praevaricationis Adae [n307] . Vides eum distinctionem fecisse perspicuam inter eos, qui similiter ut Adam, et eos, qui dissimiliter erraverant.
pass_a_gloss: Death reigned, he says, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam's transgression. You see that he made a perspicuous distinction between those who similarly as Adam, and those who had erred dissimilarly.

lemmas.lexica: LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: ‘Death reigned,’ he says, ‘even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam’s transgression’ (Romans 5:14). You see that he made a clear distinction between those who went wrong like Adam and those who went wrong differently.

choices.why: Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.
Julian: Paul says death passed to all, not sin; distinguish temporal death from eternal punishment.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
